scope: Focused implementation and output review of five symbolic narrative systems. No claim of a systematic review or exhaustive game testing.

systems.name: Curveship
systems.evidence: Executed five cases locally and read world, action, reply-planner, microplanner, example fiction, and spin code.
systems.version_caveat: The executed official Python 3 archive is version 0.6.01, with 2019/2020 port copyright dates; it is not the untouched 2011 Python 2 release.
observations: Four robbery runs change tense, narrative order, narrator/narratee, and focalization using the same fiction file.
Robbery has an explicitly authored list of twenty initial actions; these runs demonstrate retelling, not autonomous plot invention.
Default output uses vague references for unknown objects/participants, repeats the shooting event, and contains room/inventory-style exposition.

Guard telling correctly uses first person for the guard and second person for the bank teller. It still narrates brandishing before the guard wakes; no blanket claim of perfect epistemic correctness is warranted.
Artmaking executes a tiny authored puzzle: opening the box exposes the sculpture; kicking it triggers the final state.
Noninteractive execution initially failed on terminal-size detection. A runtime terminal-dimension override fixed capture without changing narrative code.

systems.name: Alabaster
systems.evidence: Played a short opening conversation in the browser (Release 3, serial 090609); inspected the archived source (associated with Release 1). Did not complete the game or rebuild it.
commands_after_intro: ask snow white about the queen
ask what the queen thinks of me
explain that I must stop here to collect the hart's heart
ask if she is a witch
observations: A broad Queen query offered specific subtopics. The chosen question produced a coherent response followed by Snow White pressing the existing pact.
The explanation for stopping connected the hart, the Queen's demand, and the mirror's limited information.
The witch question offered a follow-up; the short command ask why resolved to why people misunderstand witches.
The source separates dialogue prerequisites, direct and indirect follow-ups, repeatability, and disqualifying facts.
Two signed numerical mood dimensions map to eight named moods. The author's account says mood mainly controls expression, while knowledge primarily controls plot access.

Archived contributor tools include generating new dialogue source, fact prerequisites, and graph diagnostics; many are commented out in the release source. This is not a claim that the public release exposes an active authoring UI.
Contributor-attributed sections and editorial comments show that shared authorship still required consistency repair.
source_landmarks: source.txt lines 5070-5120: contributed dialogue, fact gating, and editorial repairs
systems.license_note: Source is available for inspection, but the game declares CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 US. This evidence packet does not reproduce or adapt its source or full prose.

systems.name: Counterfeit Monkey
systems.evidence: Played the opening and one transformation puzzle in browser Release 11, serial 260422; read selected current repository source modules. Did not complete or rebuild the game.
observations: Removing x transformed the displayed codex into a code, whose paper showed 305; setting the nearby barrier to 305 unlocked it.
Attempting to remove z from code correctly failed because the letter was absent.
The code searches an authored repository of possible objects, updates physical placement and transformation relationships, resets pronouns, and reports the new object.
Generic transformations coexist with curated objects, authored descriptions, puzzle structure, and exception rules. This is not arbitrary object creation from dictionary words.
Source comments document generation-chain collisions and fixes; this is direct evidence of interaction costs as the content library grows.

source_files.path: Counterfeit Monkey.materials/Extensions/Counterfeit Monkey/Features of Created Objects.i7x

systems.version_caveat: The maintained code and played release include later changes. The 2013 author account independently establishes the historical design.

systems.name: STORYBOOK / AUTHOR
systems.evidence: Read published output, input representation, architecture, and evaluation. Not executed; no runnable full-system distribution verified.
observations: Figure 6 reads as connected fairy-tale prose, including dialogue, scene changes, and subordinate clauses.
The evaluated planner supplied two fixed story paths; the result demonstrates prose realization rather than broad plot generation.
Paragraph-scale revision and discourse history are especially relevant to Storyweavers' event-log prose. A twenty-person ablation evaluation favored configurations retaining them.

systems.name: Versu / Prompter
systems.evidence: Read the published dinner interaction and edited Blood & Laurels scene source, plus reported limitations. Not executed; the author reported the games unavailable in 2017.
observations: The dinner example connects flirtation, departure, disappointment, altered eating behavior, and jealousy through social state.
Social practices offer possible actions; individual character preferences choose among them.
Prompter source packages dialogue in scenes with beliefs, topics, restrictions, and exit conditions.
The paper reports substantially faster authoring with Prompter, but also difficult utility tuning and conflicting concurrent practices. These are author-reported results, not reproduced measurements.

interpretation.hypothesis: Parallel coding agents may make rich, modular symbolic content affordable to author and test while runtime remains classical.
interpretation.supported_by: Actual authored knowledge libraries, explicit authoring bottlenecks, contributor workflows, and reusable rule mechanisms.
interpretation.not_established: That 10,000 independently authored modules will compose, remain readable, or produce useful training diversity. No cost or scaling experiment was conducted here.
interpretation.suggested_test: Extend one existing Storyweavers mini-adventure with reusable conversation and object modules; compare original and expanded systems on matched state cases, blind prose reading, meaningful outcome diversity, and measured integration effort.
